product_family: Espanso: A privacy-first, cross-platform text expander for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Single-product family, open-source, GPL-3 licensed, written in Rust. No commercial variants or tiers.

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance
certifications.proof_quote: no formal GDPR certification; product design is GDPR-compliant by architecture (local-only, no data collection)

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: out of scope for a text expander; not a healthcare product

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: out of scope; desktop application, no payment processing

privacy.ai_training_note: Not applicable. Espanso is a text expander, not an AI service. No cloud component, no data collection, no training.
privacy.data_region: Local only (desktop application, no cloud storage)

security.name: Architecture
security.value: 100% local operation, no cloud backend, no data collection, no tracking

security.name: Code Transparency
security.value: Open-source (GPL-3 license), full source code available on GitHub for independent code review

security.name: Binary Signing
security.value: Windows binaries code-signed via SignPath.io (third-party signing service)

security.name: Memory Management
security.value: Minimizes keylogging exposure: stores only last 5 chars by default (configurable), regex matches up to 30 chars

security.name: Vulnerability Disclosure
security.value: Report to maintainer federicoterzi96@gmail.com; no formal responsible disclosure timeline published

security.name: Key Detection Method
security.value: OS-specific APIs: RawInput (Windows), addGlobalMonitorForEvents (macOS), X Record Extension (Linux)

products.name: Espanso
products.data_scope: Local only; configuration stored in local files (~/.config/espanso on Linux/Mac, %APPDATA%/espanso on Windows)
products.notes: Desktop application for Windows, macOS, Linux. No cloud sync, no multi-device support, no account creation required. CLI-configurable or via YAML files. Extensible via packages shared on Espanso Hub.

compare.data_residency: 100% local to user's machine; no cloud storage or sync

flags: No formal privacy policy or terms of service published on website (typical for small open-source projects; not a red flag but a gap)
No enterprise security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001) - by design, as this is a volunteer open-source project, not a company
Security documentation refers to GitHub and notes docs are 'incomplete, will be updated soon' - suggests documentation maintenance is ad-hoc
Vulnerability disclosure lacks formal SLA or timeline - relies on maintainer goodwill and email response
Code-signing uses third-party service (SignPath) - acceptable, but verification chain depends on SignPath.io trust
